article.title: Building People Power Against Repression — The Black Alliance for Peace
article.content: While the outcome of this November’s historic U.S. midterm elections appears to have dealt a blow to the neofascist agenda of the Trump administration and its allies, the U.S. government’s objective in, its own words, remains full-spectrum domination. This includes the criminalization of dissent. The legal and policy architecture of this repression is codified through instruments like NSPM-7, which directs federal agencies to coordinate investigations under the banner of countering domestic terrorism and organized political violence. It draws on investigative and prosecutorial powers that successive Democratic and Republican administrations have built. Despite these electoral shifts, our task of building mass consciousness and developing independent organization based in popular power remains the same. Resistance against this repression and toward advancing the struggle for our People(s)-Centered Human Rights and collective liberation are not just strategic imperatives in the fight for human dignity and well-being, collective self-determination, and planetary survival. In part, this means building our own self-determined and alternative structures and relationships in the process of fighting against structures and systems of oppression and exploitation – locally, nationally, and globally. We do so with the firm understanding that no one can liberate another people. People liberate themselves. As such, we maintain the need for African/Black people to develop an independent radical analysis built from our own socio-historical experience, and to create a unified framework for collective struggle emanating from and defined by us collectively. Such a radical African/Black analysis takes as a starting point the need for an anti-imperialist praxis rooted in grassroots class struggle, aimed at developing class consciousness and eventually revolutionary consciousness among the masses of our people. The urgency of this moment demands a militant and strategic confrontation of imperialism, capitalism, and militarism that must be based on deeper organization, not spontaneous or sporadic action. Organizationally and politically, this requires unity and coordination in our movement in order to shore up the foundation of our base from which to strike against imperialism, support our communities and organizations, and build with the masses of our people.
